extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants (Principal Investigators), Co-Investigators, and research institution administrative staff applying to JSPS KAKENHI (International Leading Research)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures, eligibility, review criteria, research-ethics obligations, dissemination/open-access rules, and administrative requirements for applicants to the JSPS KAKENHI International Leading Research (multi-year) funding category.

rubrics_metrics.name: KAKENHI suspension periods for research misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Mapping of types/roles of individuals involved in misconduct and the degree of negative impact / maliciousness to periods of KAKENHI suspension (e.g., 10 years; 5–7 years; 3–5 years; 2–3 years; 1–2 years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table distinguishes (a) particularly malicious individuals, (b) responsible authors (corresponding/lead) vs other authors, and (c) individuals not authors; suspension periods vary by judged impact on scientific progress/social impact and maliciousness. In cases of extenuation (e.g., voluntary withdrawal of paper), suspension may be shortened as judged fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharp reprimand criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations judged subcritical to punitive suspension where a 'sharp reprimand' is administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: among certain cases where influence on society and maliciousness are judged insignificant and the amount of money involved is small; or among other case categories where influence and maliciousness are judged insignificant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of penalized researcher information to other funding agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on improper grant spending, fraudulent grant acquisition, and research misconduct may be provided to offices of other research funding agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a consequence the penalized researcher may face restrictions on application and/or participation in other competitive research funds (including proposing new projects, applying to calls, newly participating in collective research, or participating as PI or member in ongoing projects).

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional compliance with management and misconduct guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Research institutions are required to comply with the 'Guidelines on the Management and Audit of Public Research Funds at Research Institutions (Implementation Standards)' and the 'Guidelines for Responding to Research Misconduct'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If system improvement status is recognized as inadequate based on surveys, measures such as reduction in indirect costs from MEXT or controlled agencies may be taken. URLs to the two guideline documents are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of improper grant spending (misappropriation/misuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples of improper spending include: instructing a trader to forge fictitious transactions to claim purchases; obtaining false invoices with different item names; instructing students to submit false attendance sheets and pooling funds; visiting destinations not on official travel itinerary for unrelated cooperative research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: expenditures for fictitious or fraudulent transactions are considered 'misappropriation or misuse' even if intended for conducting the KAKENHI research project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraudulent grant acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquiring KAKENHI by a researcher who is ineligible (i.e., making application while ineligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of research misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include manipulation or forgery of experimental data or figures in a published research paper supported by KAKENHI; publishing translated material without prior consent or proper quotation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination: posting Research Outline and Report on KAKEN database
rubrics_metrics.description: Research achievements supported by KAKENHI are made available by posting the 'Research Outline' and 'Report on the Research Achievements' on the Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research Database (KAKEN).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable direct expenses for outreach and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Expenses for outreach-related activities, including dissemination of international research achievements by publishing papers, can be covered by direct expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees are urged to actively pursue public promotion of international research achievements using KAKENHI funds so as to make them widely known to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of KAKENHI grant in publications
rubrics_metrics.description: When publishing research achievements, researchers must indicate that the project was supported by KAKENHI by stating the JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number (JP + 8 digits) in the Acknowledgment or designated section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (English): 'This work was supported by JSPS KAKENHI Grant Number JP12K34567.' Example (Japanese) provided with JP8-digit format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution: independence of researchers' views
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications should be based on researchers' self-awareness and responsibility; they should not be presented as coming from a government request and the views should be attributed to the researchers themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example English disclaimer: 'Any opinions, findings, and conclusions or recommendations expressed in this material are those of the author(s)’ and do not necessarily reflect the views of the author(s)’ organization, JSPS nor MEXT.' Japanese example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of Open Access (OA) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS endorses general policy to promote open access for publications funded by public grants including KAKENHI, while OA is not mandatory if justifiable reasons for deferral exist (e.g., copyright issues or insufficient repository infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three main OA routes described: (i) embargoed self-archiving (institutional repository or researcher website), (ii) posting to community/public repositories, (iii) immediate OA by paying APC. Definitions of 'Embargo', 'Institutional Repository', and 'Self-archiving' are provided. URL to JSPS OA policy included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management Plan (DMP) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting from FY2024 KAKENHI call for proposals, upon formal application for grant delivery the PI of an adopted research project will be asked to make a Data Management Plan outlining storage and management of research results and research data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in line with national policies to secure research autonomy and promote open science; related policy URLs and references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct for Scientists: mandatory understanding and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must understand and practice contents of the 'Code of Conduct for Scientists - Revised Version -' (Science Council of Japan) and the JSPS booklet 'For the Sound Development of Science - The Attitude of a Conscientious Scientist'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At formal application for grant delivery, confirmation will be made via the electronic system whether PI and Co-Is have taken research ethics education coursework. URLs to the documents provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct: responsibility to assure quality and contribute to welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists shall recognize they are responsible for assuring the quality of specialized knowledge and skills they create, and for using expertise to contribute to health, welfare, societal safety/security, and sustainability of the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Basic Responsibilities of Scientists' extracted from the Code of Conduct; URL given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct: honesty, integrity, and objective demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists shall make judgments and act with honesty and integrity, endeavor to maintain and improve expertise, and make the utmost effort to scientifically and objectively demonstrate the accuracy and validity of knowledge created.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'Attitude of Scientists' in the Code; applicants must adhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct: accountability, disclosure and dialogue with society
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists shall strive to disclose and actively explain roles and significance of their research, evaluate possible effects on people, society and environment, neutrally and objectively disclose results, and build constructive dialogue with society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly emphasized as a responsibility; links provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of Conduct: dual-use awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists shall recognize that research results may be used contrary to intentions and shall select appropriate means and methods as allowed by society in conducting and publicizing research results.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Leading Research: purpose and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: enable major developments in creative/pioneering research by providing flexible large-scale long-term support for outstanding international research; expect top-level Japanese-led research groups to play central international roles, produce high international scientific value, further internationalization, advance field levels, and foster postdocs/graduate students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers significance as curiosity-driven research plus progressiveness, future potential, and competitiveness as joint international research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: PI must have internationally outstanding research results
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI must have achieved and published internationally outstanding research results; example: co-authored an international joint paper as corresponding author (published in/after 2018) ranked in top 10% most highly cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other examples of 'internationally outstanding research results' include serving as representative of a large international collaboration (e.g., spokesperson) or authoring prominent academic books published abroad and highly appraised (published in/after 2013).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: required team composition and human resource emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Research plan must be conducted by a team (PI and Co-Is) with a group of PDs and DCs as Research Collaborators; number of PDs and DCs should be approximately three times that of PI and Co-Is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard percentage of expenses for human resource development should be 70% of the proposed total budget. Mandatory initiatives: (a) plans to dispatch PDs/DCs to overseas research institutions and implement international exchanges (mainly for 2–3 years); (b) initiatives to support self-reliance of PDs/DCs (financial support allowing research with discretion and responsibility under guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Postdoctoral Fellow (PD)
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, a PD means an early-career researcher not engaged in full-time research positions: typically age 39 or under and has not acquired a Ph.D., or acquired Ph.D. within past 8 years (periods such as maternity/childcare leave excluded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Engaged in full-time research activities' refers to holding an indefinite-term appointment (e.g., professor, associate professor, assistant professor), not to working hours arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and research period limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Range of total budget: up to 500 million yen. Research period: 7 years (may be extended to maximum 10 years subject to interim assessment results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of projects to be adopted and fund allocation notes
rubrics_metrics.description: About 5 projects (highly selected) will be adopted for this category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds will be allocated to adopted projects taking into consideration, to the maximum extent possible, the full amounts requested. Additional expenses (environmental expenses, tenure start-up expenses) may be provided to foster early-career participation; details to be notified separately to PIs of adopted projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review confidentiality and reviewer obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Review is closed-door; reviewers must maintain confidentiality, must not disclose content of Research Proposal Documents or information learned during review to outside parties, must not use information for personal benefit, and must keep review materials under strict control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These obligations exist to protect applicant IP and ensure fairness of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review methods: comprehensive review structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Review comprises Document Review and Panel Review (collectively 'Comprehensive Review') conducted by section-specific committees (Humanities & Social Sciences; Science & Engineering; Biological Sciences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document Review: performed by 8–14 reviewers in principle per section, based on Research Proposal Document plus 'Review Comments' and results of 'Overseas Reviews' (about 3 domestic reviewers preparing comments and about 3 overseas reviewers). Proposals receiving extremely low marks in overseas reviews will not be adopted. As a general rule, Document Review follows a Preliminary Screening. Panel Review: committee members discuss proposals and select projects to be interviewed, then proceed with interview reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external researcher information in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers can utilize 'researchmap' and the Grants-in-Aid for Scientific Research Database (KAKEN) as necessary during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of researcher information in researchmap is referenced elsewhere in instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and disclosure of review results
rubrics_metrics.description: JSPS will notify PIs and research institutions of preliminary screening, selection for interview, adoption decisions, and provide opinions expressed in review results for adopted projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-adopted proposals, approximate ranks within each section will be disclosed via the electronic system. For proposals selected for Panel Review but not adopted, opinions expressed in review results will also be disclosed. Summaries of opinions for adopted projects will be released on KAKEN and other media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application mandatory procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Three items must be completed prior to submission: (1) Ascertain eligibility for KAKENHI application; (2) Confirm researcher information registered in the e-Rad system; (3) Obtain an ID and password for the electronic application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research institutions must perform e-Rad registration and issue IDs/passwords to PIs. Research institutions must submit a 'Self-assessment Checklist on the Implementation of the System' (based on the Management and Audit Guidelines) and a 'Checklist Pertaining to the Current Status' (based on Guidelines for Responding to Misconduct). If these checklists have not been submitted, no official grant decision will be made for researchers belonging to that institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-Investigator consent and institutional consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When composing the project team, the PI must obtain consent from prospective Co-Investigators via the electronic application system; prospective Co-Is must obtain consent from their affiliated institutions to become Co-Investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI cannot submit the Research Proposal Document to their research institution until the institutions to which the Co-Investigators-to-be belong give consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and procedural timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict deadlines for submission (example: submission to research institution and e-Rad timelines; application deadline: 4:30 pm on Wednesday, March 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines must be strictly observed; procedure steps include preparing application in electronic system, obtaining IDs/passwords (which may take ~2 weeks), and internal institutional deadlines for submitting to JSPS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim assessment and ex-post assessment process
rubrics_metrics.description: For adopted multi-year projects, an interim assessment will be conducted in the fifth year and an ex-post assessment in the fiscal year following the final year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results of interim assessments are used to determine extension of research periods, increases/decreases of funding after assessment, or termination of the project.
